simple.meaning: דְּרָאוֹן (dᵉrâʼôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an object of aversion.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Isaiah, Daniel, beginning at Isaiah 66:24. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דְּרָאוֹן (H1860).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דְּרָאוֹן (dᵉrâʼôwn) / H1860 is traced through Isaiah 66:24, Daniel 12:2 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”

timeline.evidenceText: “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”
Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

definitions.full: H1860. deraon דֵּרָאוֺן noun masculine aversion, abhorrence , absolute ׳ד Isa 66:24 object of abhorrence ; construct עולם דִּרְאוֺן everlasting abhorrence Dan 12:2 (on form compare Lag BN 200, 202 ). דרב (√ of following compare Arabic become accustomed, trained , train , compare Fl NHWB i. 444 ; also Ethiopic (quadriliteral) jaculando infigere , etc.; or, since דָּרְבָן Aramaic in form, & 1Sam 13:21 perhaps secondary, possibly regard as Aramaic loan-word & connect with Arabic be sharp, penetrating (GFM, note of Apr. 1892 )).
